thesis: Corvane proposes accelerating growth and raising gross margins by transitioning contractor ordering online through a $49/month subscription membership, AI-driven reordering, dedicated sales outreach, and branchless metro expansion.

assumptions.claim: At least 30% of Corvane's top 500 accounts will pay $49 per month for Corvane Pro delivery and bulk pricing.
assumptions.quote: We expect at least 30% of our top 500 accounts to subscribe within six months, because contractors value predictable delivery over price.

test.method: Have account reps present a binding 3-month paid Corvane Pro pilot pre-order agreement to a random sample of 50 top accounts.
test.metric: Percentage of sampled top accounts signing paid pilot agreements

assumptions.claim: Contractors are eager to migrate regular purchasing from phone and counter sales to digital self-service ordering.
assumptions.quote: Corvane's contractors are ready to move ordering online, and the company that captures that shift first will own the regional market.

test.method: Offer 100 active phone and counter buyers a $25 credit on their next order if they place it through the existing web portal instead.
test.metric: Percentage of contacted contractors who place their next order online

assumptions.claim: Historical ERP transaction data is sufficiently clean to train predictive automated cart reordering models.
assumptions.quote: Our ERP order history is clean enough to train demand forecasts that predict what each contractor will need next week.

test.method: Run an automated data audit across a sample of 10,000 recent order records to calculate product code error and duplication rates.
test.metric: Percentage of order line items with invalid, duplicate, or unmapped SKU metadata

assumptions.claim: The existing 4-person IT team possesses the availability and capability to build an AI reorder forecasting system.
assumptions.quote: Start the reorder-model build with the existing IT team.

test.method: Conduct a sprint capacity and technical skills audit with the IT lead against current ERP migration commitments.
test.metric: Available developer hours per week unallocated to the ERP migration through Q3

assumptions.claim: Corvane can hire 20 inside-sales reps during Q1 under current corporate headcount policies.
assumptions.quote: Hire 20 inside-sales reps in Q1 to call every top-500 account and sign them up for Pro.

test.method: Submit a formal hiring requisition exception request for 20 reps to executive leadership.
test.metric: Number of new inside-sales headcount requisitions formally approved for Q1

assumptions.claim: Inside sales reps will proactively drive accounts to sign up for online ordering without compensation disincentives.
assumptions.quote: Reps are the fastest path to adoption because contractors trust their branch contacts.

test.method: Ask 15 inside and branch sales reps to pitch 5 accounts each on web ordering under the current commission plan.
test.metric: Percentage of reps who actively pitch all 5 assigned accounts within one week

assumptions.claim: Contractors in new metro areas will subscribe to Corvane Pro without the presence of a local branch.
assumptions.quote: Expand to two new metro areas in the second half of the year, using Pro as the entry offer rather than opening full branches.

test.method: Run targeted search ads in one target metro driving contractors to a landing page offering next-day jobsite delivery for a $49 monthly membership.
test.metric: Conversion rate of unique contractor visitors submitting complete membership inquiry forms

conflicts.tension: The growth plan requires hiring 20 inside-sales reps in Q1, but leadership has established a company-wide hiring freeze through next fiscal year.
conflicts.quote_a: Hire 20 inside-sales reps in Q1 to call every top-500 account and sign them up for Pro.
conflicts.quote_b: A hiring freeze holds through the end of next fiscal year.

conflicts.tension: The growth plan relies on the existing IT team to build an AI reorder tool, but IT is already fully occupied with the ERP upgrade until Q3.
conflicts.quote_a: Start the reorder-model build with the existing IT team.
conflicts.quote_b: IT is fully committed to the ERP upgrade until Q3.

conflicts.tension: The growth plan assumes order history is clean enough for AI training, whereas IT found widespread duplicate and mislabeled codes in the data.
conflicts.quote_a: Our ERP order history is clean enough to train demand forecasts that predict what each contractor will need next week.
conflicts.quote_b: the team has flagged duplicate and mislabeled product codes in roughly a fifth of historical orders.

conflicts.tension: The growth strategy relies on reps driving customers online, but reps receive zero commission for orders placed online.
conflicts.quote_a: Reps are the fastest path to adoption because contractors trust their branch contacts.
conflicts.quote_b: Orders that customers place online earn reps nothing.

conflicts.tension: The growth plan asserts contractors are ready to transition ordering online, but a contractor survey indicates overwhelming preference for phone and counter ordering.
conflicts.quote_a: Corvane's contractors are ready to move ordering online, and the company that captures that shift first will own the regional market.
conflicts.quote_b: In last year's customer survey, 41 of 50 contractors said they prefer to order by phone or at the counter, mostly because they rely on branch staff to catch mistakes in their orders.
